newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday April 17.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi's government may be forced to call a confidence vote to push its 1997 mini-budget through parliament to sweep away some 1,000 amendments presented mostly by the opposition (all).

* Hard left Communist Refoundation said it wanted action against tax evasion, ten times higher in Italy than the European average, to precede any discussion by the government on welfare spending reform (all).
* Sergio Cofferati, leader of Italy's largest trade union group, said he would not discuss welfare reform with the government until it had finalised its position (all).

* Germany and France are reportedly studying a plan to pre-select countries to join EMU in the first group by September. Bonn is said to have threaten a two year delay in the start of EMU if Italy and Spain are admitted in the first wave (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi clarified recents comments that had been interpreted as suggesting the government wanted to get pension reforms started next month, and told a news conference he did not say the government wanted to carry out reforms in May. Responding to a report in the business daily Il Sole 24 Ore that a deal was taking shape between France and Germany to keep Italy and Spain out of the first wave of members of Europe's planned single currency, the minister said there were no "secret deals" (all).

* A report by national statistics institute ISTAT showed Italian producer prices rose 0.8 percent year-on-year in February compared with an increase of 0.9 percent in January. ISTAT also reported wholesale prices rose 0.5 percent in February against 1.0 percent in January (all).
* State broadcaster RAI and state telecoms holding STET said they planned a strategic alliance to develop a common digital standard for satellite and cable communications in Italy (all).

* Financial holding company IFI saw parent company net profit up 50 percent at 80 billion lire in 1996. IFI said its 1996 net consolidated profits were in line with the 411 billion lire seen in 1995. The Agnelli family holding company also confirmed that it held directly some 99.6 percent of the share capital in Juventus, one of Italy's leading soccer teams (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* Spanish Banco Santander, IFI, Italian banks IMI and Monte dei Paschi di Siena and insurer Reale Mutua Assicurazioni will become core shareholders in San Paolo bank, which will be privatised later this year (all).

* Shares in information technology group Olivetti were temporarily suspended after a sharp fall following the group's release late Tuesday of 1996 and first quarter 1997 results and a share capital reduction plan (all).

* A report by Italian Banking Association ABI showed the rate of growth in total Italian bank lending slowed in March but foreign currency loans showed an increase. ABI chairman also said interest rates should continue falling at least until June due to a drop in inflation and only slight signs of economic recovery (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
